data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate experienced an overall gross prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 209.4 million in 2021, representing 8.46% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This movement was primarily driven by adverse development in certain financial lines classes, partially offset by positive developments across other classes. General factors influencing reserve estimates include changes in claims incidence, volatility in long-tail classes, catastrophic events, legal environment changes (including Ogden rate), and social/economic trends like inflation. The Syndicate also noted continued benefits from lower attritional claims experience in some portfolios due to lockdown periods, which could contribute to favourable prior year development.

Volatility in the estimation of future costs for long tail insurance classes due to the longer period of time that elapses before a definitive determination of the ultimate claims cost can be made
Incidence of catastrophic events close to the balance sheet date

Changes in the legal environment, including the interpretation of liability laws and changes in methodologies to estimate the quantum of damages including changes to the Ogden rate and interpretation of business interruption policy coverage
Social and economic trends, for example price and wage inflation and interest rates
